Exercise C.S30 — Hard: Ranks, ties and marginal coverage
      
        There are $19$ exchangeable calibration scores and one future score, all distinct almost surely. A prediction rule accepts the future point when its score is at most the $18$th smallest calibration score. Find its marginal acceptance probability. Why need this not be $90\%$ for each subgroup?
        Review if needed: this section and conditional probabilities.
        
          Show hint
          Among all $20$ scores the future score has a uniform rank. Compare that rank with $18$.
        
        
          Show worked solution
          Exchangeability and absence of ties make the future score's rank uniform on $1,\dots,20$.It is at most the $18$th calibration score exactly when its overall rank is at most $18$. Hence acceptance probability is $18/20=0.9$.This averages over calibration data and the future point. For example, two equally common subgroups with conditional coverages $0.8$ and $1$ also average to $0.9$. Marginal coverage alone does not guarantee either subgroup's target, or conditional coverage for the observed calibration set.

hypotheses: All20 calibration-plus-future coordinates have a genuine jointly exchangeable probability measure, invariant under every coordinate permutation; all20 scores are distinct almost surely. This joint assumption is stronger than exchangeability of only the19 calibration coordinates.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The definition is actual joint-law permutation invariance. The proof derives uniform rank from equal coordinate rank probabilities and the a.s. one-per-rank indicator sum, rather than assuming uniform rank.

Actual acceptance is equivalent to zero-based overall rank<18; finite disjoint rank-event probabilities give18/20=.9, under the explicit joint-exchangeability assumption.

reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The actual measure has subgroup masses.5/.5, acceptance joint masses.4/.5 and marginal.9; genuine cond computes.8/1. This suffices for the asserted numerical subgroup counterexample and weighted averaging, without assuming subgroup target equality.

hypotheses: The actual uniform measure on all permutations of Fin20 yields jointly exchangeable distinct coordinate scores. The observed ordered calibration vector0,...,18 is a measurable positive-probability singleton-permutation event.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The actual exchangeable tie-free permutation-score experiment has marginal acceptance.9, but conditional on the genuine positive-probability observed calibration vector the remaining future score19 is rejected and conditional acceptance is0. This proves the exact non-guarantee for observed-calibration conditional coverage.
